transcript.content: Hello, it’s nice to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi, nice to meet you too. Um, I came in because... well, recently I was working on a memorial piece for my aunt. I do art for a living, so I'm used to second-guessing my work, but this was different. I kept getting these really awful, unwanted thoughts that I was going to dishonor her somehow. 

It was like, if I made just one wrong photo placement or picked the wrong color, it meant I didn't love her enough. I just couldn't brush them off like my normal creative doubts, and it really bothered me.
When these thoughts came up, did you feel driven to do something repeatedly to make sure you had not dishonored your aunt?

Yeah, I did. Um, I would end up rereading the label text for the piece over and over. And I'd keep... just nudging the same objects around on my work table, or checking the layout photos repeatedly. I basically had to keep doing all that until things finally felt, I don't know, settled. 

It's really frustrating because part of me knows the piece is already fine, but I feel like I have to do it anyway, and I just end up losing a lot of good studio time.
Do these unwanted thoughts and repeated checking behaviors occur only with the memorial piece, or do they also happen in other areas of your life?

Um, no, not really. It seems to just be with the memorial piece. I mean, I always double-check my artwork before I finish it, but that just feels like normal perfectionism, you know? 

This specific thing—where I feel like I have to keep checking or else it means something terrible—I haven't really noticed that happening in any other part of my life. It's really just been with this one project for my aunt.
Did these unwanted thoughts and checking behaviors begin after your aunt’s death or another specific stressful event?

Um, I'm not entirely sure. I mean, her passing was obviously a difficult time, but I don't know if I'd say that's exactly what started it. I didn't really notice these kinds of thoughts until I actually sat down to start working on the memorial piece recently. 

I haven't really noticed it being tied to any other specific stressful events, either. It just sort of... began when I started this particular project.
Since your aunt’s death, have you been experiencing significant emotional distress in areas of your life outside working on the memorial piece?

No, not really. I mean, I miss her, obviously, and it's sad, but I'm functioning fine otherwise. I'm seeing my friends, doing my normal daily stuff, paying my bills... I'm not, like, falling apart or anything. The distress is really just focused on this one art piece.
About how much time each day do you spend rereading, rearranging, or checking things for this memorial piece?

It's hard to put an exact number on it, but it definitely adds up. I’ll end up rereading the label text, nudging the same objects on the table, and checking the layout photos over and over again. I just keep doing it until it finally feels 'settled' in my head. Even though, logically, part of me knows it’s already fine and I’m really just losing valuable studio time, I just can't seem to stop until it feels right. I'd say it takes up a good chunk of my time when I'm trying to work on it.
How long have these unwanted thoughts and checking behaviors been happening?

Um, I'm not exactly sure of the timeframe, to be honest. Like I mentioned, it really just started when I began working on the memorial piece. So... however long that's been. I haven't really kept track of the exact days or weeks. It just sort of crept up on me once I got deep into this specific project.
How long before you began the memorial piece did your aunt die?

She passed away about... hmm, I guess it was a few months before I actually started working on the piece. I took some time first, just to process things, before I felt ready to start putting the memorial together.
Have these unwanted thoughts and repeated behaviors been happening continuously for at least two weeks?

Um... I would say yes. I haven't exactly been marking it on a calendar or anything, but it feels like it's been at least a couple of weeks. Ever since I really got into the thick of this project, it's been happening pretty much every day I'm in the studio working on it.
Did the unwanted thoughts and checking behaviors begin within three months after your aunt died?

Um, I'm not entirely sure on the exact timeline. Like I said, she passed away a few months before I started the project... but whether the checking and the thoughts started exactly within that three-month window after she died, I really couldn't say for certain. I just know it all kind of started when I began working on the memorial.
What do you feel would happen, or what feeling comes up, if you tried to stop checking before the piece felt completely settled?

If I try to stop, I just get this overwhelming feeling that it's wrong, like the piece isn't right yet. So I'll end up rereading the label text, or... nudging the exact same objects on the table, just a fraction of an inch. And I'll keep checking the layout photos over and over until it finally feels 'settled.' Even though, logically, part of me knows it's already fine and I'm just wasting valuable studio time doing it.

Before your aunt died or before you began this memorial project, had you ever experienced similar unwanted thoughts that led you to repeat checking, arranging, or other behaviors until things felt right?

No, I really haven't. I mean, I've always been a bit of a perfectionist with my art—making sure the lighting is right or the composition works—but it was never like this. I never had these kinds of thoughts or felt like I had to keep checking the exact same thing over and over just to get rid of a bad feeling. This is all new, really just since I started working on this specific project.
Approximately how many months after your aunt’s death did the unwanted thoughts and checking behaviors first begin?

I really don't have an exact number for you. Um, like I mentioned a little bit ago, I just didn't keep track of the timeline like that. There was a gap between when she passed away and when I actually started working on the memorial piece... but I honestly couldn't tell you exactly how many months that was. I just know the checking started as soon as the project did.
Did the unwanted thoughts and checking behaviors first begin within three months after your aunt died?

I'm really not sure if it was within three months. Um, it could have been, or it might have been a bit longer than that. I just didn't keep track of the time. Like I said, I only know for sure that it started when I actually began putting the piece together.
How much have these thoughts and checking behaviors interfered with completing the memorial piece?

I mean, I’m still getting most of my work done, so it hasn't completely stopped me. But... the extra time I lose in the studio because of all this checking definitely adds up. It actually already cost me a grant deadline. And, um, I even had to back out of a gallery talk that I had really wanted to do, just because I was so behind. So it's definitely interfering more than I'd like.
Do you recognize that the fear of dishonoring your aunt and the need to keep checking are excessive or unreasonable, even while you feel unable to stop?

I mean, yes, I know it doesn't make sense. I know checking the materials over and over isn't actually going to change anything or somehow make the piece more respectful. I can see that it's too much, but... I just can't seem to stop myself from doing it anyway. It's like I have to do it just to get the thought out of my head.
When you reread, rearrange, or recheck the piece, are you doing those actions specifically to reduce the distress caused by the fear that you might dishonor your aunt?

Yes, that's pretty much it. I'll end up rereading the label text, or... nudging the same objects on the table, and checking the layout photos over and over. I just keep doing it until it finally feels settled and that fear goes away. Even though part of me knows it's already fine and I’m really just losing my studio time, I have to do it to get that relief.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient reports recurrent, unwanted, distressing fears of dishonoring her aunt, accompanied by repetitive checking, rereading, and arranging behaviors performed to reduce distress and achieve a sense of completeness. She recognizes the thoughts and behaviors as excessive, cannot resist them, and experiences clinically significant occupational impairment. The symptoms have persisted for at least several weeks. A circumscribed trigger does not exclude obsessive-compulsive disorder; adjustment disorder and obsessive-compulsive personality disorder are less consistent with the ego-dystonic, ritualized, newly emergent symptoms.

confirmed_symptoms: Recurrent unwanted thoughts that an incorrect artistic choice would dishonor her aunt
Marked distress associated with the fear that the memorial piece is wrong or insufficiently respectful
Recognition that the fear is excessive or unreasonable
Repeatedly rearranging or nudging the same objects on the work table
Continuing the behaviors until the piece feels settled
Performing the behaviors specifically to reduce distress and obtain relief
Understands that repeated checking will not objectively improve the piece or make it more respectful
Identifies the checking behaviors as excessive while feeling unable to stop

diagnostic_checklist.duration_verified: Symptoms have occurred on most studio-working days for at least a couple of weeks; exact onset and total duration were not established.
additional_requirements: Obsessions and compulsions are linked: compulsions are performed to reduce distress from the obsessional fear
Symptoms are ego-dystonic and resisted to some degree
Clinically significant occupational impairment confirmed by lost studio time, a missed grant deadline, and withdrawal from a gallery talk
No comparable prior history of obsessions or compulsions reported
